newsitem.title: USA: Ford shifts corporate ad agencies.
newsitem.headline: Ford shifts corporate ad agencies.

text.p: Ford Motor Co said on Wednesday that it dropped Wells Rich Greene BDDP as its corporate advertising agency after 16 years and has moved the estimated $70 million account to Ogilvy & Mather.
Wells Rich Greene is owned by GGT Group Plc. O&M is a unit of WPP Group Plc.

Ford spokesman John Ochs said the move is part of an effort by the U.S. No. 2 automaker to create global marketing efficiencies. He would not confirm industry estimates that value the account at $70 million.
"This is part of Ford's ongoing move to align itself with global suppliers, including primary advertising agencies, to achieve important synergies and marketing efficiencies," said Ochs.

O&M currently handles advertising for Ford's U.S. customer service division, Ford of Europe, and Ford's Jaguar luxury car account in both the U.S. and Canada. The agency will take over February 5, 1997. Ochs, who wouldn't disclose further details of the switch, said the decision was made "in recent days." It comes almost two months after Ford hired James Schroer as executive director of its newly created Marketing Strategy and Brand Management Office.

Schroer was given responsibility for developing Ford's global marketing, brand strategies, and for creating a consistent Ford brand image worldwide. The move marked the second time one of Detroit's Big Three automakers hired an outsider to reshape its brand image. Schroer most recently worked for consulting firm Booz, Allen and Hamilton. General Motors Corp has also been hiring vehicle brand managers from outside of the auto industry.
Wells Rich Greene is responsible for developing the "Quality is Job One" slogan used in Ford Motor corporate ads.
